finding.claim: POST /profile/avatar fetches an attacker-supplied URL with axios. The only check is startsWith('https://'), which does not restrict host, IP, or redirects, so the server can be made to request internal or link-local addresses. Response is blind: only byte length is returned.

trace.note: url = req.body.avatarUrl taken directly from request body
Validation: typeof string and startsWith('https://') only; no host/IP allowlist
URL passed unchanged to axios.get; axios follows redirects by default (up to 5, protocol switch allowed), so an https:// URL can redirect to http://169.254.169.254 or other internal addresses
Only img.data.length is returned as { bytes }, making the SSRF blind; errors become unhandled rejections

finding.guards_checked: Type check and https:// prefix (server.js:11): do not restrict destination host/IP, do not block redirects. No private/link-local IP blocking, no DNS-rebinding protection, no redirect limit, no timeout, no response size cap, no try/catch around axios call. Redirect-to-http bypass based on axios defaults; not executed/verified at runtime.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is server.js:11 (typeof string plus startsWith('https://')), which is a prefix/scheme-only check and does not close the finding. No auth middleware is registered (server.js:5 is express.json only), and nothing limits redirects, IPs, or hosts before the sink at server.js:14.
verdict.reason: The handler at server.js:9 is unauthenticated, req.body.avatarUrl at server.js:10 flows unchanged past the https:// prefix check at server.js:11 into axios.get at server.js:14, and nothing in the path restricts destination host or IP. The redirect behavior relies on axios defaults (follow-redirects, maxRedirects 5, which permits https-to-http), which I did not verify against the installed axios version because there is no package.json or lockfile here.
